facts.text: United was founded in 1881 when the United Coal & Coke Company opened the United Mine and Coke Works in Mount Pleasant Township.
The town grew around a rail link: the United Mine connected to the Sewickley Branch of the Southwest Pennsylvania Railroad, moving coal and coke to Pittsburgh.
By 1886, United Coke Works housed 300 bee‑hive coke ovens, producing nearly 134,000 short tons of coke that year.
Frick Coke Company took full control of the United Mine in 1895, expanding the site to 350 coke ovens and employing 341 men and boys.
The landscape still shows scars from mining: abandoned tipples and deteriorated coke oven batteries stand amid regrowing vegetation.
United sits on the eastern slopes of the Allegheny Front, where its elevation shapes local drainage and creates a distinctive microclimate.
